Vowels are traditionally omitted in standard writing, though dots and dashes called *niqqud* are added in children's books, poetry, and religious texts to show vowel sounds.[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wQLwNbeuAJM)[[2]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Introduction/Basic_Features/basic_features.html)\n- **Final Letters:** Five letters (*kaf, mem, nun, peh, tzade* ) change their shape when they appear at the very end of a word (called *sofit*).[[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ekc3lIVdHEU)[[2]](https://hebrew4christians.com/Grammar/Introduction/Basic_Features/basic_features.html)\n- **Script Evolution:** Modern Hebrew uses the square block script (derived from Aramaic-style script), while ancient texts were written in Paleo-Hebrew.
